newsitem.title: USA: Analysts split on Raytheon recovering in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Analysts split on Raytheon recovering in Q4.

text.p: Analysts who track Raytheon Co, which reported lower operating income in the third quarter, are split on whether the Lexington, Mass-based contractor will be able to recover in the fourth quarter.

The company earlier reported delays in financing for its Engineers & Constructors division, weakening sales in its appliance division and an eight-week strike all contributed to a $75 million shortfall in operating income. The earnings per share price will not be directly affected, analysts said, because the company intends to use a $75 research & design tax credit to offset the loss.

"I've lowered my earnings per share by a nickel for the year," said JSA Research Inc, analyst Paul Nesbit, who also said that the cut to $3.60 from $3.65 eps was due to the weakness in the appliance sector.

"Raytheon always has a strong fourth quarter," he said. "Sales of aircraft always increase, and I fully expect the financing for the Engineering & Constructors division to come through, but I don't expect the appliance part to recover."
But James Pierce of PNC Institutional Investors Services, said he expected the fourth quarter earnings per share to reflect the "spillover from lagging sales in appliances.
"I think it will be a down fourth quarter," he said. Pierce said he rated Raytheon a market performer and intended to keep that rating on the stock.
Nesbit, who rates the company a strong buy, said the sharp 3-3/4 drop in price 49-1/4 in late trading "makes it even more attractive."
